ingredients:
Peaches
Syrup, water, or juice
Ascorbic acid solution (optional for preventing darkening)
instructions:
1. Dip fruit in boiling water for 30 to 60 seconds until skins loosen. Dip quickly in cold water and slip off skins.
2. Cut in half, remove pits and slice if desired.
3. To prevent darkening, keep peeled fruit in ascorbic acid solution (1 teaspoon ascorbic acid powder per gallon of water OR crush and dissolve six 500-milligram vitamin C tablets per gallon of water). Drain.
4. Hot pack - In a large saucepan place drained fruit in syrup, water, or juice and bring to boil.
5. Fill jars with hot fruit and cooking liquid, leaving ½-inch headspace. Place halves in layers, cut side down.
6. Raw pack – Fill jars with raw fruit, cut side down, and add hot water, juice or syrup, leaving ½-inch headspace.
7. Adjust lids and rings.
8. Process in a boiling water canner.
9. After processing, take canner off heat. Remove lid and wait 5 minutes before removing jars.

recipe_name: Whole or halved tomatoes, packed raw without added liquid
ingredients:
Whole or halved ripe tomatoes
Acid (lemon juice or citric acid)
Salt (optional)
instructions:
1. Prepare tomatoes by dipping in boiling water for 30 to 60 seconds or until skins split. Dip in cold water and slip off skins. Remove cores.
2. Leave tomatoes whole or halve them.
3. Loosely fill jars with raw tomatoes, pressing until spaces fill with juice.
4. Leave ½ inch headspace.
5. Add acid: 2 tablespoons bottled lemon juice or ½ teaspoon citric acid per quart jar (half these amounts for pint jars).
6. If desired, add salt: ½ teaspoon per quart or ¼ teaspoon per pint.
7. Adjust lids and process in a boiling water canner according to processing time and altitude (see below).

ingredients: Wash beans and trim ends. Leave whole or cut into 1-inch pieces. Add salt, if desired (½ teaspoon per pint; 1 teaspoon per quart).

3. Remove air bubbles.
4. Wipe rims and adjust lids.

ingredients:
7 lbs. of 2 - to 2 - ½ - inch diameter beets
4 to 6 onions (2 - to 2 - ½ - inch diameter), if desired
6 cups apple cider or white distilled vinegar (5%)
1 - ½ teaspoons canning or pickling salt
2 cups Splenda® (optional)
3 cups water
2 cinnamon sticks
12 whole cloves
instructions:
1. Wash and rinse pint canning jars; keep hot until ready to use. Prepare lids according to manufacturer's directions.
2. Trim off beet tops, leaving 1 inch of stem and roots to prevent bleeding of color. Wash thoroughly. Sort for size. Cover similar sizes together with boiling water and cook until tender (about 25 to 30 minutes). Caution: Drain and discard liquid.
3. Cool beets. Trim off roots and stems and slip off skins. Slice into 1/4 - inch slices. Peel, wash and thinly slice onions.
4. Combine vinegar, salt, Splenda®, and fresh water in large Dutch oven. Tie cinnamon sticks and cloves in cheesecloth bag and add to vinegar mixture. Bring to a boil. Add beets and onions. Simmer 5 minutes. Remove spice bag.
5. With a slotted spoon, fill hot beets and onion slices into clean, hot pint jars, leaving 1/2 - inch headspace. Cover with boiling hot vinegar solution, leaving 1/2 - inch headspace. Remove air bubbles and adjust headspace if needed. Wipe rims of jars with a dampened clean paper towel; apply two - piece metal canning lids.
6. Process in a boiling water canner according to the recommendations in the table below. Let cool, undisturbed, 12 to 24 hours and check for seals.

instructions:

7. Adjust lids and process in a boiling water canner according to the chart.

ingredients:
Raw tuna
Optional: ½ teaspoon salt per pint or ¼ teaspoon per half-pint
Optional: small pieces of belly fat
No added liquid or oil is necessary
instructions:
1. You may can tuna either raw or precooked. Precooking removes most of the oil that tends to have a strong flavor; however, many people find it easier to can the tuna raw in its own juices.
2. When you can raw tuna, it is easier to fillet the fish when it is partially frozen. You can skin raw tuna before or after filleting. It is not necessary to remove the viscera before filleting.
3. For either raw or precooked tuna, peel off the skin with a sharp knife. Scrape the surface lightly to remove blood vessels and any other discolored flesh.
4. Separate the fish into quarters by cutting meat away from the bones. Pull off and cut out all bones and fin bases. Scrape and cut out all the very dark flesh as this has a stronger flavor which can affect the delicate tuna flavor.
5. Cut fish loins crosswise with a sharp knife into lengths suitable for jars.
6. Pack pieces into hot half-pint or pint jars, pressing down gently to make a solid pack. A small piece of belly fat can be added to each jar to enhance the flavor and texture of the meat.
7. Salt or other spices are optional. Use ½ teaspoon salt per pint or ¼ teaspoon per half-pint as a good flavor.
8. Leave 1 inch headspace between top of fish and jar. No added liquid or oil necessary.
9. Wipe the jar rims clean with a paper towel moistened with vinegar to remove any oil from the tuna before putting on the lid and rings.
10. Tighten rings snugly but do not overtighten to avoid buckling of lids during processing.
11. Process in a pressure canner following manufacturer's instructions. Exhaust steam for 10 minutes before pressurizing. Start timing when recommended pressure is reached. Maintain pressure and process for 100 minutes.
12. After processing, remove canner from heat and let pressure return to zero.
13. Remove weight or slowly open petcock. Wait 10 minutes before opening lid and removing jars.
14. Allow jars to sit undisturbed for 12 hours before testing seals.
15. Remove rings for storage. Store jars in a cool, dark, dry place. Use within one year for best quality.

Clean cloth or paper towels (to wipe rims)
Large pot or bowl for preparing food

checklist.title: Pressure canning checklist
checklist.note: Processing time __ minutes at __ pounds pressure (adjust for altitude).
steps: 2–3" water in canner (3–4" if fish) — 140°F raw pack, 180°F hot pack
When timing complete, remove from heat, wait
When fully depressurized, remove weight or open petcock
Store in cool, dark, dry place
Wash and dry canner, gasket and lid
